summary.one_liner: An awesome-list of Python typing resources, covering type checkers, runtime checkers, stub packages, typing helper libraries, tools, editor integrations, PEPs, and articles.
summary.what_it_does: This is a curated link list rather than a software project. It is organized into sections: static type checkers (mypy, pyright, ty, pyrefly, and others), dynamic/runtime type checkers (beartype, typeguard, pydantic, and others), stub packages (django-stubs, boto3-stubs, sqlalchemy-stubs, and others), and additional types such as Result/Option libraries. It also covers backports (typing-extensions, future-typing), tools grouped into linters, testing plugins, "working with types" utilities, and annotation helpers like monkeytype and pyannotate, plus mypy plugins and editor integrations. The final sections list the relevant PEPs (484, 544, 589, 612, and others) and third-party articles and tutorials.
use_cases: Finding a static type checker for a Python project
Choosing a runtime type validation library
Locating type stubs for a third-party library
Adding type annotations to an existing codebase
Setting up mypy or pyright in an editor
Reading background on PEP typing features
notable: Covers static checkers, runtime checkers, and stub packages in separate sections
Lists annotation-generation tools such as monkeytype, pyannotate, and RightTyper
Includes PEP links and third-party tutorials on typing topics
Points to a 'Related' list of other type checker resources
caveats: It is a link collection, so it has no installable code and each entry's status, maintenance, and license must be checked on its own project
Entries are not verified for currency; some tools are listed alongside newer or older alternatives
keywords: add type hints to existing code
